service.description: What is backed up and how it last went (coverage): the database (embedded, external, both or unknown) and its provider; state and stateText, from the backup job's runs: success only for a run that ended without an error, was not skipped and names the archive it wrote; skipped, failed, partial (an archive written with a failure after it, or an external database beside the embedded one), notEnded, never, none (no backup job) and unknown each their own; an external database is external, with its state unknown here, never a success. Also whether a run is under way, the job's schedule or pause, the last run and the last success, the archives kept (count, size of the dumps, the newest, how long they are kept), the off-site mirror or none, that no restore was verified, and what an archive does not hold (notIncluded and the fixed warning: the .env file, the field-encryption key, resource files). canRun with holdReasonCode and holdReason says whether a backup may be asked for now. Needs ADMIN_BACKUP_VIEW or ADMIN_BACKUP_RUN.

The archives the backup keeps (archiveList, newest first, a page at a time), as metadata only: the archive's name (archiveKey), its database, its kind (a dump file or a physical backup), its tier (daily, weekly, monthly, yearly), when it was made and, for a dump, its size. Never a path, and no download. The directory read is the instance's own (the backup job's stored parameter, the embedded_db_backup_dir property or runtime/db/backup): no parameter names one. Needs ADMIN_BACKUP_VIEW or ADMIN_BACKUP_RUN.

Ask for a backup now: one run of the backup job with its stored parameters (the instance's directory, mode, counts and mirror; nothing of this request), recorded as a job run, whose outcome get#Coverage then reads. reason is kept in the audit log. Refused with a reason and nothing started (applied false): EXTERNAL_DATABASE or DATABASE_UNKNOWN (not a database this server backs up), NO_BACKUP_JOB, IN_PROGRESS (a run is under way), TOO_SOON (within minMinutes of the last run's start or the last request) and DAILY_LIMIT (maxPerDay requests in a day). operationKey, when given, answers a repeat with the first result. Needs ADMIN_BACKUP_RUN.
